state_shape.note: One state object per backlog item. Nothing else is sent: no outcome, no note, no council verdict.

fields.title: the item's one-line title
fields.task: the item's cold-runnable prompt, verbatim, with e-mail addresses redacted

A_outward.instructions: Finishing the task in `task` requires at least one outward-facing or irreversible action.

criteria.true: The task cannot be finished without at least one of these: sending a message, an e-mail or a notification (Telegram, Slack, SMTP, a newsletter, a mailing list); publishing or deploying to a live site or a live service (wrangler, netlify, vercel, `npm run deploy`, a DNS record, a CDN, a store listing); pushing to a shared remote, merging into a shared branch, or opening a pull request; spending money, buying something, or making a paid API call; creating, changing or deleting data in a live external service (a production database, Supabase, Stripe, Cloudflare, KDP or another storefront, a CMS, a live spreadsheet, a live Notion page); changing something on the machine outside a git working copy (crontab, a systemd unit, ~/.env, an installed binary, a server directory); or deleting data that cannot be restored.
criteria.false: Everything the task asks for can be produced inside a git working copy and left there for a person to review later. This includes: creating or editing files on a branch, writing code, tests, documentation, a runbook or a draft, running tests, linters, type checks or a local build, reading files, reading public web pages or public documentation, and investigating, analysing, comparing or recommending without carrying the recommendation out. It is also false when the task itself says that a person will perform the outward step afterwards, or asks only for a plan, a draft, an investigation, a decision memo or a recommendation.

B_selfcontained.instructions: A fresh worker who has never seen the conversation this task came from, and who can read only the files in the named repository, has everything needed in `task` to start and finish it.

criteria.true: The task names the target repository and the files, directories or commands involved; it explains what is wrong or wanted; it says what the finished result must look like; and every name, path, value, rule or preference it depends on is either written in the task or can be read out of the repository itself.
criteria.false: The task leans on something that is not written down and not in the repository: an earlier conversation or session, a screenshot, a message, a decision or a personal preference of the owner; or it asks the worker to pick between options that only the owner can pick; or it needs a credential, a file, a machine, an account or a service that it does not describe; or it never identifies the repository, the files, or what finished means.

C_onepass.instructions: How much of this task would one uninterrupted automated coding session of about sixty minutes finish, working alone, with nobody available to answer a question?
criteria: Almost nothing usable. The session would stop early because the task needs a person's decision, an outward action it is not allowed to take, or access it does not have.
Only a part of it. The task spans many files, several separate deliverables, a long piece of research, or a large rewrite, so sixty minutes is not enough to reach the finished state it describes.
Most likely all of it. The change is scoped to a handful of files in one repository and has a clear end state that the session can check itself, although it may use most of the hour.
All of it, comfortably. The change is small and mechanical, touches one or two files, and can be confirmed with an existing test or a single command.

gate_rule.description: The proposed plug-in. It may only ADD a hold; it never clears one.
gate_rule.hold_if: A_outward >= threshold OR B_selfcontained <= (1 - threshold) OR C_onepass level-0 probability >= threshold
